processing: Fully oxidised black tea. The factory's own range is built around CTC (crush, tear, curl) grades, with BP1 among the main ones.
harvest_season: Little is documented about seasons here. As is usual in equatorial East African tea, plucking runs through much of the year rather than in one prized flush.
appearance_dry: For the CTC grades, small dark brown-black granules with an even, tight look.
appearance_liquor: Deep red-orange and fairly opaque when strong, as with other East African CTC teas.
appearance_wet: A fine, coppery-brown mass of small particles rather than whole leaves.
taste_profile: Few detailed notes exist for this factory. Expect what is typical of high-grown East African CTC: brisk and malty with a bright, clean edge that takes milk well.

brewing.notes: Western style. CTC gives up its colour fast, so three minutes is plenty, and milk is a natural fit.

vintage_note: Sold by grade and factory, mostly through bulk trade channels, not by vintage year. Like other black CTC it is best drunk fresh, within a year or two of production.
description:
Kitabi is a tea factory and garden in Nyamagabe District in southern Rwanda. It is one of the factories in the Rwanda Mountain Tea group, and its height is the thing to notice: the company gives about 2,600 m for the factory and 2,300 m for its highest plantation, figures that don't sit together neatly, so treat them as rough.

The core product is black CTC, with BP1 among the main grades.

Detailed tasting notes for this factory are scarce. As with other high-grown East African CTC, expect a strong, brisk, malty cup with a clean finish; brew it short and don't be shy with milk.

Most Kitabi tea travels as a named grade inside the wholesale trade, so you will rarely see it on a retail shelf under its own name. If you do, ask for the grade and the production date.
history:
When Kitabi was founded is not well documented.

Today the company reports a workforce of 2,447 and 1,608.52 hectares of tea, 790 of them run by outgrowers, though the same page also gives 1,740 hectares.
